restrictions: Ordinary collisions of the complete sha3-256-r5-prefix-v1 hash (zero IV, prefix rounds 0..4, SHA3 padding, full 256-bit digest); outputs are two distinct 135-byte messages.
Deterministic algorithm, no random coins, executed to completion: success probability 1. Cost = cost of that execution.

Phase A: exhaustive enumeration of CP-kernel alpha_3 of Hamming weight <= 10 with exact slice-local filters, then a CP-SAT feasibility screen (connector load w1 <= 140) in generation order, stopping at the first feasible survivor (position 159); outputs Guo et al. Trail core No. 3.

Phase B: exact 2-round connector solved by single-worker CP-SAT with deterministic-time limits only and lazy relation cuts; seeds 100, 101, ... in order; seed 100 succeeds (DF 52), reproduced bit-identically.

Phase C: fixed chunk-major Gray-code enumeration of a 38-dimensional subspace of the connector space until the first digest collision, at index 122745632515; replayed by an organizer-executed experiment.
Costs: permutation calls 1 unit; own C code by explicit operation counts; CP-SAT and Python by hardware-counted retired instructions x 1024 (H3); OS time charged at a ceiling rate x 1024.

heuristics.statement: Every retired ARM64 instruction of the black-box CP-SAT/Python processes in Phases A2 and B is simulated by at most 1024 collision-frontier-v5 word-RAM primitives, so retired instructions x 1024 bound their charged work.
heuristics.scope: Phases A2 and B as executed (Apple M4 Pro, OR-Tools 9.15, Python 3.14); instruction counts from the process hardware counter; kernel work charged separately at a ceiling rate.
heuristics.extrapolation: From per-instruction-class emulation bounds (load/store, ALU, multiply, divide, IEEE double operations, 128-bit SIMD, CRC32) to every instruction executed; the instruction mix itself was not measured.
heuristics.limitations: A worst-case argument, not a measured instruction mix; it likely overstates cost. An instruction class needing more than 1024 primitives would invalidate the factor for that class.

heuristics.statement: The reported instruction counts are the costs of the deterministic executions of Phases A2 and B on the stated platform and software versions; re-execution reproduces the same computation up to a small count spread.
heuristics.scope: Phase B executed twice with bit-identical output and a measured instruction-count spread; Phase A1 counter-based operation bound matches its hardware count.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the replicated runs to the stated single executions of A2 and B on the same platform and versions.
heuristics.limitations: Other platforms or library versions execute different instruction streams and may take different solver paths; the claim is tied to the stated execution.
